title: Java Day 2: Install JDK and set up your editor

scenes.heading: Java Day 2
scenes.narration: Welcome to Java, day two. Yesterday you saw how Java runs a program. Today we get your computer ready. Do not worry, we will go one step at a time, and you will not feel lost.

props.title: Java Day 2
props.subtitle: Install JDK and set up your editor

scenes.heading: What is the JDK
scenes.narration: First, what is the JDK? Think of it as a toolbox. It has everything you need to write Java code and run it. Without this toolbox, your computer does not understand Java at all.

scenes.heading: Parts of the JDK
scenes.narration: Inside the JDK there are two main parts. The first is javac. It is the compiler. It reads your code and checks it. The second is the JVM, the Java Virtual Machine. It runs your finished program.

scenes.heading: Why we need it
scenes.narration: Why do we need this? Imagine trying to cook without a stove. You could try, but it would be very hard. Without the JDK, you cannot compile Java code or run it. The toolbox makes both steps simple.

scenes.heading: Today's map
scenes.narration: Here is the full map for today. First, download the JDK. Next, install it. Then check it in the terminal. Last, open an IDE and write your first code.

scenes.heading: Download the JDK
scenes.narration: Step one. Go to the official Adoptium website. Choose the latest LTS version. LTS means long-term support, so it stays stable for years. Then download the installer for your system.

scenes.heading: Your first code
scenes.narration: Now a tiny Java file, so you can see what code looks like. Read it slowly. The word class names your program. The main method is where Java starts running your code.

scenes.heading: Line three
scenes.narration: Look at line three. This line prints text on the screen. System dot out dot println means print this. The words inside the quotes are what you see when the program runs.

scenes.heading: Compile and run
scenes.narration: Now run it. First type javac Hello dot java to compile. Then type java Hello to run it. If you see Hello, Java on the screen, your setup works. That is a win.

scenes.heading: Check the install
scenes.narration: Before that, check your install. Type java dash version in the terminal. You will see a version number. Yours may be different from this one, and that is fine.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.narration: Here is a common mistake. You see command not found. This means your computer cannot find Java yet. Usually, you just need to close and reopen the terminal after installing, so it can find the new path.

scenes.heading: Choose an IDE
scenes.narration: Next, choose an IDE. An IDE is your writing desk for code. IntelliJ IDEA is great for Java. VS Code is light and free, with a Java extension. Pick one, and stick with it for this course.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.narration: Let us recap. The JDK is a toolbox for Java. javac compiles your code, and the JVM runs it. Install the latest LTS version, then check it with java dash version. Pick one IDE.

scenes.heading: Practice task
scenes.narration: Your practice task for today. Install the JDK. Run java dash version. Write your version in the comments. Stuck? Tell me the error message, and we will fix it together.

scenes.heading: See you
scenes.narration: That is day two. You now have a Java toolbox and an editor. Next lesson, we write our first real program. See you tomorrow.
